author: GamingBolt
description:
Supermassive’s upcoming Directive 8020 is all about high-stakes, consequence-driven gameplay - and while this is very much in the vein of what the developer is used to, it looks like an ambitious step forward regardless. 

The deep space setting is perfect for the themes of isolation and despair, and the narrative is all about branching choices and how those will come to haunt you in the finale. With great visuals and an appropriately haunting score, Directive 8020 is packed with potential that Supermassive can capitalize on to develop something that’s highly engaging and highly replayable.
title: Why Directive 8020 Could Be One of the Biggest Games Of The Year

author: GamingBolt
description:
We’ve had some time with Saros, we thought it a good idea to give you a rundown of what to expect from its performance on both the PS5 and PS5 Pro. That’s exactly what we’ve got in store for you with this one, as we dive into how the game handles its revised approach to its presentation, combat, and Carcosa’s new atmosphere.

You’ll be happy to know that it’s all good news if you’re thinking about diving into this one, and you’re going to want to see how it manages to be a step-up from Returnal which was an already solid offering from Housemarque to begin with. How does Saros up the ante, then? Join us and find out.
title: Saros PS5 Pro vs PS5 Graphics Comparison - Yet Another Visual Masterclass From PlayStation

author: GamingBolt
description:
When I first laid hands on Saros, it felt like everything I ever wanted, and then some, especially after waiting for so long. Having spent an extensive time with it, I don't have that same sense that every single little desire of mine was met, but that's perfectly fine when confronted with such a robust experience with some of the best third-person shooter gameplay, combined with a nuanced bullet hell system and progression that feels consistently rewarding. 

I lost count of the number of times my jaw was left agape, either due to the environmental wonders before me or from the many memorable encounters against its enemies. The fact that I keep returning, even though the story is essentially wrapped, may be a curse in some ways. It probably means I've already begun the inevitable wait for the threequel, and to see what terrible new loop Housemarque has planned next.
title: Saros Review - The Final Verdict
